evidence: src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService gets ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports through its constructor, so it does no direct persistence work
placeOrder hands stock changes to the domain functions reserve and release, and its try/catch rollback coordinates an all-or-nothing use case across several products
advance and cancel hand state rules to the domain functions nextState and assertCancellable
placeOrder checks input: lines.length === 0 and Number.isInteger(line.quantity) — a borderline invariant that could live in a domain Order factory, but is acceptable as use-case validation
The file has no HTTP, routing, serialization or storage code
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
OrderService is a use-case service. Its methods are placeOrder, getOrder, listOrders, advance, cancel and the stock queries. Each one loads data through injected repository ports, calls domain functions, and saves the result. That is the job of the application layer. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, file or storage access) and no transport code (no HTTP requests or responses, status codes or serialization). Framework code is limited to node:crypto randomUUID for generating IDs, a small technical detail that is normal in a use case.

Some rules sit here that a stricter domain-driven design would move into a domain Order factory:
- an order must have at least one line
- each quantity must be a positive integer
- lines for the same product are merged
- the status is set directly (order.status = next / "cancelled")

These are borderline, not misplaced. Checking input and coordinating the all-or-nothing reservation with rollback across several products are reasonable application tasks. The main state rules are already delegated to the domain: nextState, assertCancellable, isOrderStatus, reserve, release, dispatch and toStockLevel. Nothing here belongs to a different layer kind, such as infrastructure in this file or business rules in an infrastructure file, so the file passes. Confidence is moderate because of the anemic-domain smell around order construction.
